name: smoke-sar-bias
description: Harness acceptance test: ideal divider + 3.3 V MOS bias + sampling-switch Ron. Not a SAR ADC.
claim: None — harness self-verification, not a spec claim. Proves the PVT plumbing (vdd_val substitution, MOS .lib corner sections, .temp) actually takes effect, so later records against ratified spec lines (#1) can be trusted.

vdiv_ratio.description: an ideal divider is exactly vdd/2 at every PVT point — the invariant control. If this moves, the harness is perturbing something it should not.

vdiv_abs.description: the same divider in absolute volts must track the supply (±10% ⇒ ~20% spread) and must NOT move with process or temperature. Proves vdd_val substitution reaches the netlist and is the only thing the V axis changes.

vgs_nfet.description: diode-connected nfet_03v3 Vgs at 10 uA. The per-axis floors prove the MOS .lib section changes between corners AND that .temp is applied — a grid-wide floor alone would pass with either one stuck.

ron_switch.description: sampling-switch on-resistance at Vgs=vdd. The three-axis sensitivity prover: process (mobility/Vth), temperature (mobility), supply (overdrive). If any of these floors is not met the corner runner is not moving that axis.

vres.description: unsalicided poly divider tap — proves the resistor .lib sections take effect for the bias/reference device class.

isup_ua.description: total supply current stays sane at every corner

notes: Harness acceptance testbench. The per-axis sensitivity floors here are the repo's guard against a corner runner that silently simulates typical everywhere; `sim/selftest.sh` re-runs this testbench with `--sabotage-corners` and requires it to FAIL.
